chapters.title: A dry umbrella
panels: Rain reaches The Proving Ground just as its hand-drawn map goes missing.
An umbrella stands by the door, perfectly dry beneath a wet hook.
Mira finds a map pin in the umbrella's handle.
Dev recalls moving the map indoors when the first clouds gathered.
The indoor wall is bare, but a rectangle of dust shows where paper rested.
A canteen tray carries a faint outline of the map's square corners.
On Sunday, the map turns up beneath the tray. One path has been redrawn in silver ink, ending at a locked garden gate.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals a tiny umbrella sketched at the gate's far side.

chapters.title: The silver path
panels: The silver path avoids a puddle no mapmaker could have known about yesterday.
Mira learns the garden keeper had warned visitors of a leaking tap.
The keeper's warning note never reached the notice board.
Its paper is pinned behind a schedule for the courtyard workshop.
The workshop leader says she moved the note to keep the schedule dry.
Dev follows the silver path and finds the tap already repaired.
On Sunday, the keeper shows them the repair log. It bears a signature dated one day before the leak was found.
chapters.bonus: The bonus panel reveals the log page was reused from an old notebook.

chapters.title: The earlier date
panels: The date belongs to an old seed order on the back of the page.
Mira holds it to the light and sees two kinds of ink.
The repair was logged today, just as the keeper said.
The odd silver path was made by a student planning a dry route for visiting children.
That student used foil from the workshop to mark the path.
The children arrive and follow it with delight, counting every turn.
On Sunday, their count stops one turn early. A narrow walkway is missing from both the old map and the new one.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals the walkway hidden under an arch of jasmine.

chapters.title: A way through
panels: The jasmine arch leads to a small bench facing the rain garden.
No sign marks the bench, though its wood is newly polished.
The keeper says the bench was made for anyone needing a quiet minute.
Dev checks his map and leaves the bench unnamed, as the keeper asks.
Mira suggests a gentle symbol instead: a little open circle.
The children draw their own circles and add places where they felt welcome.
On Sunday, the map is covered in circles. One appears beside a door everyone thought had been sealed.
chapters.bonus: The bonus panel shows a neat keyhole in that door's frame.

chapters.title: The open circle
panels: The door leads to a store of spare tables, not a secret room.
A round table sits at the back, still wrapped from last year's fair.
Its label says 'for maps that change'.
Mira carries it into the courtyard when the rain eases.
Visitors add routes, benches and helpful taps to a fresh sheet.
Dev pins the old map beside it, dated and thanked for all it got right.
On Sunday, the first new map is complete. In one corner, a child has drawn a road that leaves the page.
chapters.bonus: The boss board reveals the road leads to the next village's shared library.
